title: Sanctions & Impact
public_rule: Understand the plumbing at analyst depth. Show the reader which valve got closed, what stopped flowing, what still flows around it, and why they should care.

governing_rules.designation_is_not_damage: A legal designation establishes that a restriction was imposed. It does not by itself prove that money stopped moving, trade stopped, or the target lost access to every workaround.
governing_rules.legal_reach_is_not_behavioral_reach: U.S. law does not directly prohibit every foreign transaction. Practical reach expands when foreign banks, insurers, shippers, suppliers, and payment firms change behavior to protect access to U.S. finance, markets, or counterparties.

why_now.lead: Iran has lived with U.S. sanctions in changing forms since 1979. The wartime campaign shown here is different because it increasingly targets the financial and commercial routes around Iran as well as Iranian actors themselves.

points.title: Older sanctions often left usable detours.
points.text: Iran built workarounds through exchange houses, front companies, smaller banks, local-currency settlement, shipping intermediaries, and third-country trade.

points.title: Wartime measures increasingly name the detours too.
points.text: Treasury actions during the war have reached exchange houses, foreign financial institutions, aviation and procurement intermediaries, maritime insurance structures, crypto platforms, industrial suppliers, and other facilitators.

points.title: Secondary sanctions turn legal pressure into business pressure.
points.text: A foreign firm may not be directly forbidden from every Iran-linked transaction, but it can still decide the business is not worth risking access to U.S. banks, dollar clearing, suppliers, or customers.

points.title: The effect is cumulative, not magical.
points.text: Closing one route rarely ends the flow. The pressure comes from reducing clean alternatives, increasing screening and delay, raising cost, and making each remaining workaround easier to identify.

before.label: Long-running pressure
before.text: Sanction Iranian institutions and sectors while Iran develops detours through intermediaries and third-country trade.

now.label: Wartime network pressure
now.text: Sanction Iranian targets, identify the facilitators and settlement routes, and pressure foreign institutions that keep those routes commercially usable.

definitions.plain: The bank-to-bank relationships that let a bank send money internationally when it does not have its own branch in the other country.
A non-U.S. bank or business may be outside a direct U.S. ban, but certain Iran-linked activity can still cost it access to U.S. finance, markets, or other U.S.-linked business.
A company can be treated as blocked when sanctioned people or companies own 50 percent or more of it in the aggregate, even if that company is not separately named.

core.label: Iran
core.sublabel: Oil sales, imports, procurement and state-linked finance

intermediaries.label: Trader / front company
intermediaries.explanation: Can disguise the Iranian counterparty or commodity chain; naming the facilitator raises screening and ownership risk.

intermediaries.label: Exchange houses
intermediaries.explanation: Move currency outside ordinary bank channels; wartime actions have targeted exchange networks used by sanctioned Iranian banks.

intermediaries.label: Shipping / insurance
intermediaries.explanation: Cargo can move only if ships, brokers and coverage remain commercially available; sanctions can make a formally possible voyage unattractive.

intermediaries.label: Foreign bank / correspondent
intermediaries.explanation: A foreign bank may pull back if Iran-linked business threatens correspondent access or creates unacceptable compliance risk.

alternatives.label: Digital-asset route
alternatives.explanation: Still a workaround, but Treasury has increasingly named exchanges, developers and facilitators.

alternatives.label: Local-currency / barter route
alternatives.explanation: Can reduce dependence on dollar clearing, but does not remove shipping, banking, ownership, supplier or secondary-sanctions risk.

legend.blocked: Legal or commercial route unavailable in the cited case
legend.degraded: Still possible, but with materially more friction or reduced availability
legend.usable: A remaining route; not a claim that it is cheap, safe, or sanction-proof
legend.high-risk: Increased screening, counterparty, ownership, or secondary-sanctions exposure

cascade.title: One facilitator is named
cascade.text: The legal action identifies a node that was helping an Iran-linked flow.

cascade.title: Screening expands
cascade.text: Banks and businesses check ownership, counterparties, payment paths and connected companies more closely.

cascade.title: Banks pull back
cascade.text: A bank can reject or delay transactions even when no authority physically prevents the payment.

cascade.title: Insurers and suppliers reassess
cascade.text: The same risk spreads into cargo cover, shipping, trade finance, parts and services.

cascade.title: The route becomes expensive or toxic
cascade.text: The transaction may still be possible, but fewer firms will touch it and the remaining path costs more time, money and risk.

sanctions_types.plain: U.S. persons and transactions under U.S. jurisdiction are directly restricted by the applicable Iran sanctions rules.
Certain non-U.S. dealings can trigger U.S. consequences even when the foreign company is not itself American.

map_nodes.name: Iran — sanctioned financial and industrial base
map_nodes.note: Represents the Iranian institutions, sectors and state-linked financial activity targeted by the sanctions program.

map_nodes.name: UAE — banking and aviation exposure
map_nodes.precision: Country-level jurisdiction marker; not an office location
map_nodes.note: Treasury targeted Iran-linked access through a UAE bank in August; by September the UAE aviation authority publicly implemented the U.S. aviation restriction for Iranian airlines.

map_nodes.name: Türkiye — financial facilitators
map_nodes.note: Treasury targeted financial lifelines and facilitators in Türkiye as part of the wartime campaign.

map_nodes.name: Russia — VTB Bank
map_nodes.precision: City-level jurisdiction marker; not an office-level pin
map_nodes.note: Treasury designated VTB for Iran-related sanctions evasion, including alleged correspondent relationships and settlement channels with sanctioned Iranian banks.

map_nodes.name: Iraq — aviation and trade pressure
map_nodes.precision: City-level jurisdiction marker; not a facility location
map_nodes.note: Iraq became part of the observable implementation story when Iranian flight access was restricted during the September aviation-sanctions rollout.

map_nodes.name: China — major oil and trade relationship
map_nodes.note: China remains economically important to Iran; the map marks exposure and remaining trade capacity, not a claim that Chinese trade has stopped.

wartime_actions.title: Supreme-leader financier and shadow exchange houses targeted
wartime_actions.targeted_node: Financial facilitator, exchange houses and shell-company layers
wartime_actions.function: Move funds for sanctioned Iranian banks and regime-linked actors outside ordinary transparent banking channels.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: OFAC designated the named financier and exchange-house network.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: The designation establishes legal pressure on the named network. This record does not by itself prove that all associated money flows stopped.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: Banks, exchanges and counterparties connected to the network face greater screening, ownership and sanctions exposure.

wartime_actions.title: IRGC procurement network targeted
wartime_actions.targeted_node: Foreign aviation, transport and financial conduits
wartime_actions.function: Obscure IRGC involvement while moving material, money and personnel for procurement.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: OFAC designated seven individuals and entities in the international procurement network.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: The action names specific procurement intermediaries; disruption to every downstream procurement route is not assumed.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: Suppliers and financial intermediaries dealing with connected actors face greater sanctions and compliance risk.

wartime_actions.title: Hormuz insurance and shadow-fleet network targeted
wartime_actions.targeted_node: Maritime insurance and service entities tied to the Strait
wartime_actions.function: Collect maritime payments and provide an IRGC-linked service layer around passage through Hormuz.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: OFAC designated firms Treasury described as integral to the maritime insurance/extortion scheme.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: The named service and payment structure became a sanctions target. The action does not prove that every vessel or every Iran-linked maritime payment stopped.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: Shipowners, brokers, insurers and payment firms have stronger reasons to avoid the named structure and connected counterparties.

wartime_actions.title: Crypto and clandestine currency networks targeted
wartime_actions.targeted_node: Digital-asset exchanges, front companies and shadow-currency facilitators
wartime_actions.function: Move and obscure value outside ordinary bank channels and obtain foreign currency for state-linked actors.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: OFAC designated exchanges and facilitators Treasury linked to IRGC and sanctions-evasion activity.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: The named platforms and networks became directly exposed to sanctions. Digital assets remained a workaround category rather than disappearing.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: Exchanges, wallet services and counterparties become easier to screen out once the network is named.

wartime_actions.title: Foreign-bank access pressure widened
wartime_actions.targeted_node: UAE banking access and Iran-linked financial actors
wartime_actions.function: Provide foreign-bank and correspondent access for Iran-linked financial activity.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: Treasury proposed restricting Banque Misr UAE's U.S. correspondent access and sanctioned additional Iran-linked financial actors.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: This moved the campaign beyond Iranian institutions into the foreign banking layer. Separate evidence is still required to measure transaction losses caused by the action.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: Foreign banks must weigh Iran-related business against access to U.S. correspondent relationships and the broader dollar system.

wartime_actions.title: Aviation network and intermediaries targeted
wartime_actions.targeted_node: Iranian airlines, foreign intermediaries and procurement/transshipment routes
wartime_actions.function: Move aircraft, parts, technology, personnel and cargo through aviation and procurement networks.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: Treasury sanctioned 36 targets and suspended Iran-related aviation authorizations.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: By September 24, the UAE aviation authority suspended Iranian airline operations to and from the UAE and cited the U.S. ban; Reuters also reported cancellations elsewhere. Worldwide grounding was not established.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: Foreign airports, service companies, suppliers, lessors and banks may withdraw from Iran-linked aviation to avoid sanctions exposure.

wartime_actions.title: Russia's VTB Bank targeted for Iran-related sanctions evasion
wartime_actions.function: Treasury alleged VTB maintained Iran offices, correspondent relationships with sanctioned Iranian banks, rial-ruble settlement channels and efforts involving frozen Iranian assets.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: Treasury designated VTB under an Iran-focused authority.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: The previously announced large-bank action became an enacted designation. The available accepted record does not quantify how much Iranian settlement volume stopped as a result.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: The action raises the cost and risk of using large foreign banks as durable substitutes for sanctioned Iranian banking channels.

wartime_actions.title: Military procurement networks hit again
wartime_actions.function: Obtain weapons and components for Iran's defense sector through overseas commercial networks.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and entities in multiple jurisdictions under Operation Economic Outcast.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: The named procurement nodes were exposed and sanctioned. Loss of every alternate supplier or procurement route is not established.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: Suppliers and payment channels connected to the identified network face greater screening and transaction risk.

wartime_actions.title: Industrial suppliers and the A7 financial network targeted
wartime_actions.targeted_node: Automotive, rail, manufacturing, steel and financial-network facilitators
wartime_actions.function: Support industrial supply and move state-linked money through an intermediary network.
wartime_actions.legal_effect: OFAC expanded sectoral and entity sanctions across Iranian automotive, rail, manufacturing and steel networks and related foreign suppliers. Separately, OFAC sanctioned the A7 Network; FinCEN issued an alert and proposed—not finalized—a rule that would prohibit covered fund transmittals involving A7 Sub-Agents.
wartime_actions.observed_effect: The October 1 legal perimeter widened again. OFAC's A7 designation took effect, while FinCEN's Sub-Agent transaction restriction remained a proposed rule at this evidence cutoff; neither action by itself establishes a quantified economy-wide loss.
wartime_actions.potential_effect: More supplier and payment relationships can become commercially unattractive as connected foreign firms assess U.S. financial and sanctions exposure.

observed_effects.title: Regional aviation pullback became visible
observed_effects.text: The September aviation campaign produced concrete regional implementation: the UAE aviation authority suspended Iranian airline operations to and from the UAE, while Reuters reported additional cancellations. The evidence does not establish a complete global grounding.

observed_effects.title: Indian exports faced additional friction
observed_effects.text: Reuters reported that India's exports to Iran were expected to fall further as a Dubai transshipment route was halted and U.S. sanctions pressure increased.

observed_effects.title: Oil and foreign-currency pressure intensified alongside the blockade
observed_effects.text: Reuters reporting in early September described sharper pressure on Iranian oil exports and the wider economy from the combined blockade and sanctions campaign. The blockade and sanctions are not treated as interchangeable causes.

remaining_routes.title: Local-currency settlement
remaining_routes.text: Avoiding dollars can reduce direct dependence on dollar clearing, but it does not erase sanctions on the banks, owners, goods, shippers or counterparties involved.

remaining_routes.title: Barter and commodity settlement
remaining_routes.text: Goods can be exchanged without a normal dollar payment, but the physical trade still needs suppliers, logistics, insurance and counterparties willing to accept the risk.

remaining_routes.title: Digital assets
remaining_routes.text: Crypto can move value outside conventional bank rails, but exchanges, developers, wallet infrastructure and facilitators can themselves be identified and sanctioned.

remaining_routes.title: Front companies and smaller intermediaries
remaining_routes.text: Layering ownership and using smaller facilitators can obscure a transaction, but each newly identified intermediary gives banks and suppliers more names, ownership links and patterns to screen.

remaining_routes.title: Third-country banks and trade hubs
remaining_routes.text: A foreign bank may remain legally able to conduct some business yet still retreat because access to U.S. correspondent banking, counterparties or markets matters more than the Iran-linked transaction.

watch.label: Foreign-bank pullback
watch.text: More banks reducing or ending Iran-linked business, correspondent ties or settlement services.

watch.label: Rial and FX pressure
watch.text: Whether foreign-currency access becomes harder and more expensive rather than merely volatile.

watch.label: Import friction
watch.text: Longer settlement times, disrupted transshipment, supplier exits or difficulty paying for ordinary imports.

watch.label: Procurement difficulty
watch.text: Evidence that sensitive or dual-use parts take longer, cost more, or require more layers of intermediaries.

watch.label: Workaround substitution
watch.text: Whether trade shifts into local currency, barter, crypto, smaller banks or new front companies rather than disappearing.
